title: Adaptive Sandbox Recipes: inline, executable onboarding cards for cost & rollout teaching
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: new users land on a blank dashboard or rollout view and lack contextual steps to learn cost controls, rollout policies, and preview outcomes. Proposal: ship a set of 'Sandbox Recipes' — compact, adaptive cards embedded in empty states and first-touch surfaces that are prefilled with runnable configurations (eg. simple model route, batching settings, and a mock traffic profile). Recipes execute in-place against a safe demo environment, show projected cost/latency trade-offs, and let users apply the configuration to their own project or save as a template. Goals are to reduce time-to-value, lower support asks about cost and rollouts, and increase adoption of best-practice defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Three recipe categories implemented: 'Cost Saver', 'Low-latency Pilot', 'Canary Rollout'
Cards appear in Dashboard and Rollouts empty states when user has no prior configs
In-place execution uses demo tokens and returns realistic simulated metrics (latency, tokens, projected cost)
CTA to 'Apply to project' creates a draft route/config in the user's workspace
Analytics fire for card views, runs, and Apply actions
design_notes: Cards are single-row, 320px width min, compact visualizations (sparkline for latency, cost donut) and a short 1-line summary
Adaptive content: copy and default values vary by detected user persona (engineer vs product manager) and by detected account tier
Accessibility: keyboard focus, ARIA labels for run/apply actions, and colorblind-friendly palette required
Non-goals: this feature does not replace in-depth tutorials or paid templates marketplace
Data privacy: demo runs never access customer keys; 'Apply to project' requires explicit consent and uses the customer's configuration but not live traffic
